hero.headline: Trump says Iran peace deal stalled as negotiations continue
hero.body:
President Trump said Iran has not agreed to a deal to end the ongoing conflict because the country is strong and proud, but indicated Tehran will ultimately have to reach an agreement. "They're strong, they're proud, there are things they never thought they'd be doing that they're going to have to do," Trump said, suggesting Iran has no choice but to accept terms in negotiations aimed at ending hostilities between the United States and Iran.

The president acknowledged the difficulty of the diplomatic process without specifying what leverage or circumstances would force Tehran to the negotiating table. Trump stated the deal would either be "great and meaningful, or there will be no deal at all."

Iran's negotiating team has taken a more cautious stance about the talks. Esmail Baghaei, the spokesperson for Iran's negotiating team, said that while negotiators have reached conclusions on many issues, an agreement is not imminent. "It is correct to say that we have reached a conclusion on a large portion of the issues under discussion. But to say that this means the signing of an agreement is imminent – no one can make such a claim," Baghaei said at a foreign ministry press briefing.

Baghaei also pointed to confusion in American positions and Israeli interference as obstacles to reaching a deal. He insisted that a ceasefire in Lebanon must be included in any memorandum of understanding that would lead to Iran allowing commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the United States lifting its blockade of Iranian ports. Regarding the strait, Baghaei clarified that discussions centered on "fees for navigational services" rather than tolls.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed more optimism about the negotiations. "There were some talks going on in Qatar today, so we'll see if we can make progress. I think it's a lot of talking back and forth going on about specific language in the initial document," Rubio told reporters in Jaipur during an official visit to India. He added that the Strait of Hormuz would open "one way or another."

The conflict between the United States and Iran has created significant diplomatic and logistical challenges extending beyond the negotiating table. These complications have affected international events, including the World Cup, which begins Thursday. FIFA declined Iran's request to relocate its group stage matches from U.S. stadiums to venues in Canada or Mexico.

Iranians are largely banned from traveling to the United States under current restrictions. The Iranian soccer team will have to fly in and out of the country for each match without overnight stays, creating an exhausting schedule for the three group stage games on U.S. soil.

The negotiations represent a test of whether diplomatic channels can resolve the conflict between Washington and Tehran while addressing the humanitarian and logistical consequences of the ongoing tension.

cards.headline: 12 people shot at Ohio street festival, suspects still at large
cards.body:
At least 12 people were wounded in a shooting near the Old West End Festival in Toledo, Ohio on Saturday, with two victims in critical condition. Police are continuing their search for the individuals responsible.

The gunfire erupted near the busy street festival, causing attendees to scramble for cover while others assisted the injured. According to Toledo police, it appears that two people fired weapons at each other during the incident.

Police have not yet released detailed information about the conditions of the other 10 victims beyond those in critical condition. Authorities have also not indicated whether the shooting was targeted or occurred randomly during the community gathering.

The Old West End Festival is an annual event held in Toledo's historic neighborhood. It attracts many residents and visitors to the area each year. The shooting prompted Toledo officials to urge the public to submit any videos or photos of the incident to help with the ongoing investigation.

Law enforcement described the level of violence as extreme. The FBI set up a tip line to gather information from the public about what happened and to help identify the suspects involved. Police have not disclosed additional details about what may have prompted the shooting.

The incident adds to a troubling pattern of mass violence at public gatherings across the United States in recent years. Festivals and outdoor community events have become increasingly vulnerable to such attacks, raising concerns about security measures at celebrations. Ohio has experienced multiple mass shootings recently, including the 2019 Dayton shooting that killed nine people and wounded many others.

Authorities continue their active investigation as they work to identify and apprehend the suspects. Police are asking anyone with information about the shooting to contact them or the tip line. The community is being encouraged to cooperate with law enforcement by providing any evidence that might assist in solving the case.

The shooting has prompted discussions about safety at public events and what security measures might be implemented to protect attendees at future festivals and gatherings. Officials are working to determine the circumstances that led to the violence and to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.

As the investigation continues, police say they will provide updates as more information becomes available. The two victims in critical condition are receiving medical treatment for their injuries.

cards.headline: Russian drone strikes nuclear fuel storage facility near Chornobyl
cards.teaser: A Russian drone hit a building storing spent nuclear fuel near the Chornobyl nuclear plant, Ukrainian officials said.
cards.body:
A Russian Shahed drone struck a building at the spent nuclear fuel storage facility near the disused Chornobyl nuclear power plant. The reception building of the storage facility sustained substantial damage, though it was empty of fuel containers at the time of the attack.

President Zelensky condemned the strike as deliberate and "extremely vile," criticizing it ahead of scheduled talks in London. The targeting of the sensitive site appears intended as a message from Moscow amid an intensifying exchange of long-range aerial strikes between Russia and Ukraine, with both sides hitting high-profile locations.

cards.headline: OPEC Plus Raises Oil Output Despite Strait of Hormuz Closure
cards.teaser: The cartel plans to increase production by 188,000 barrels daily as the Iran conflict continues to disrupt shipping.
cards.body:
OPEC Plus announced a plan to increase oil production by 188,000 barrels per day even as efforts to reach a ceasefire in Iran stalled. However, the cartel's move is largely symbolic because the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil transport, has stranded vast quantities of petroleum and severely limited market access.

Rising oil prices have triggered concerns about demand destruction—a sustained loss of demand caused by elevated prices. Goldman Sachs has warned that global oil demand faces significant headwinds, raising questions about the cartel's production increase amid these economic pressures.

cards.headline: Trump does not rule out paying January 6 rioters who attacked police
cards.teaser: President Trump declined to rule out providing payouts from an anti-weaponization fund to January 6 defendants who assaulted law enforcement officers.
cards.body:
President Trump declined to rule out providing payments from a proposed anti-weaponization fund to January 6 defendants who attacked police officers. The fund would compensate individuals Trump believes were unfairly prosecuted.

More than 140 police officers were injured during the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack. Trump has previously called some January 6 defendants "hostages" and has pardoned several convicted of riot-related crimes.

cards.headline: Federal and local agencies track anti-tech extremism as AI backlash grows
cards.teaser: The FBI and Department of Homeland Security are monitoring anti-technology extremism, while Philadelphia police admit to tracking First Amendment activity critical of artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
Philadelphia police have acknowledged monitoring First Amendment activity critical of artificial intelligence. The FBI and Department of Homeland Security have identified opposition to rapid technological change, particularly AI, as a potential driver of political violence.

Recent incidents have fueled law enforcement concern. A 20-year-old Texan was arrested for allegedly attempting to burn down OpenAI's headquarters and Sam Altman's house, with an anti-AI manifesto found among his possessions. An Italian Instagram influencer was charged with plotting anti-tech attacks inspired by Ted Kaczynski, while perpetrators of a deadly mosque attack in San Diego also cited opposition to AI. Civil liberties advocates have raised concerns about surveillance targeting constitutionally protected speech and assembly.

cards.headline: Trump Discusses Government Stake in AI Companies
cards.teaser: The administration is considering plans to give Americans equity in artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump said a potential U.S. government equity stake in major AI companies could be beneficial, with discussions planned for the coming week. The administration is exploring how the government might acquire and distribute ownership stakes in artificial intelligence firms, allowing Americans to benefit financially from AI's success.

Senator Bernie Sanders has proposed that citizens own half of AI company equity as a public resource. Several approaches are being considered for how the government could structure such ownership arrangements.

cards.headline: Gunman kills one and wounds five in central Israel attack
cards.teaser: Israeli authorities described the shootings in central Israel as a terrorist attack, with at least one person killed and five wounded.
cards.body:
A gunman opened fire in central Israel, killing one person and wounding five others in what Israeli authorities characterized as a terrorist attack. The shooter was identified as an Arab Israeli by Israeli media. Hamas praised the assault but did not claim responsibility for the attack.

The shooting took place in a populated area of central Israel. Israeli security forces responded to the scene and are investigating the circumstances of the attack. The incident adds to ongoing security tensions in the region as Israeli authorities work to determine the shooter's motives and any potential connections to militant groups.

cards.headline: Hundreds freed from Boko Haram hideout in Nigeria
cards.teaser: Nigerian forces freed hundreds of captives, including many women and children, from a Boko Haram mountain hideout.
cards.body:
Nigerian security forces rescued hundreds of captives from a Boko Haram mountain hideout. The freed group includes many women and children who were abducted in March from an area near the Cameroon border.

The March abduction had drawn international attention to the militant insurgency in northeastern Nigeria. The rescue operation marks a significant recovery effort by Nigerian forces against the group.

cards.headline: Peru holds presidential runoff election amid voter discontent
cards.teaser: Peruvians voted in a tight presidential runoff between candidates representing the left and right, with insecurity and instability driving voter concerns.
cards.body:
Peru held a presidential runoff election between two candidates representing opposite political poles. Keiko Fujimori, daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, faced leftist congressman Roberto Sánchez. Fujimori advanced from the first round with 17% of the vote, while Sánchez secured 12%, narrowly ahead of ultra-conservative Rafael López Aliaga.

The election reflected deep voter frustration with Peru's persistent crises. Rising crime, corruption scandals, and severe political instability dominated the campaign, as Peruvians sought a president capable of addressing these urgent issues. The race marked the country's ninth presidential election in a decade, underscoring the instability voters hoped the next government would finally resolve.

cards.headline: Pope Leo draws 1.2 million to Madrid Mass focused on poverty
cards.teaser: Pope Leo told a crowd of 1.2 million people in Madrid that God stands with the poor during an open-air Mass.
cards.body:
More than a million people gathered at Madrid's Plaza de Cibeles for an outdoor Mass led by Pope Leo, marking his first papal visit to Spain in 15 years. Crowds lined the streets as the pontiff arrived in his popemobile, with attendees waving flags and cheering "Long live the pope" as flower petals were tossed in his path.

During the Mass, Pope Leo emphasized God's solidarity with the poor and called on world leaders to stop dividing electorates and respect every human being. The visit comes as Spain experiences political polarization, with some conservative groups distancing themselves from the church. The massive turnout underscores the enduring strength of Catholic devotion in the country.

cards.headline: Hegseth criticizes Europe over migration in D-Day anniversary speech
cards.teaser: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth attacked Europe over migration policy during a D-Day anniversary speech in Normandy, drawing condemnation.
cards.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used a D-Day commemorative speech in Normandy to criticize European migration policies, describing immigration as an "invasion" of Europe's shores. Speaking 82 years after the allied liberation operation, Hegseth connected the historical anniversary to contemporary immigration debates.

The remarks drew sharp condemnation from historians and rights campaigners, who accused him of "grotesque stupidity" and desecrating the memory of soldiers who died in the Normandy landings. Critics objected to politicizing a solemn historical commemoration focused on wartime sacrifice and allied cooperation.

cards.headline: Iran World Cup team arrives in Mexico amid US visa dispute
cards.teaser: Iran's national soccer team landed in Mexico as a visa dispute complicates their World Cup participation, with all group games scheduled in the US.
cards.body:
Iran's World Cup team arrived in Mexico to prepare for the tournament, with all three of their group-stage matches scheduled in the United States. A visa dispute has complicated their participation, with players and coaching staff approved for entry on June 5, but several support staff members reportedly denied visas, including Iranian football federation chief Mehdi Taj.

The team will need to fly in and out of the US for each match day rather than staying throughout the group stage. Iran opens their World Cup campaign on June 15 against New Zealand in Los Angeles. The visa row reflects broader diplomatic tensions between Iran and the United States.

cards.headline: Simone Biles discloses recent health scare
cards.teaser: Olympic gymnast Simone Biles revealed she experienced a health emergency that she described as almost dying.
cards.body:
Seven-time Olympic champion Simone Biles revealed she experienced a serious health emergency that required hospitalization. She described the incident as "almost dying," sharing a photo on Instagram showing multiple hospital bracelets on her wrist. The 29-year-old gymnast noted the experience was one of the scariest of her life.

Biles said she would provide more details about the medical emergency at a later date. She emphasized that she typically values her privacy but felt compelled to share news of the incident publicly.

cards.headline: Five arrested after protests over fatal stabbing in Southampton
cards.teaser: A 16-year-old girl is among five people arrested following disorder in Southampton near where Henry Nowak, 18, was fatally stabbed.
cards.body:
Five people, including a 16-year-old girl, were arrested during disorder that broke out in Southampton on Tuesday near where 18-year-old Henry Nowak was fatally stabbed. Three of those arrested have since been charged.

Foreign Secretary David Lammy rejected Vice President JD Vance's suggestion that the killing was linked to mass migration, telling Vance his comments were incorrect.

cards.headline: Iran national team based in Mexico for World Cup amid visa dispute
cards.teaser: Iran's World Cup team landed in Mexico and will fly in and out of the United States on match days for their group stage games.
cards.body:
Iran's national soccer team has established its World Cup base in Mexico despite all of their group stage matches being scheduled in the United States. The arrangement stems from visa complications affecting several members of their delegation.

Players and coaching staff received visa approval on June 5, though some support staff were reportedly denied entry. As a result, the team will fly into the United States on match days for their games, then return to Mexico. Iran opens their tournament on June 15 against New Zealand in Los Angeles. The team had previously trained in Turkey while working to resolve the visa issues.

cards.headline: One million attend papal Mass in Madrid
cards.teaser: A crowd of one million gathered in Madrid for a Mass celebrated by Pope Leo, the first papal visit to Spain in 15 years.
cards.body:
More than a million people gathered near Madrid's Plaza de Cibeles for an outdoor Mass led by Pope Leo. Crowds lined the streets waving flags and shouting support as the pope arrived in his white popemobile, with some attendees tossing flower petals in celebration.

This marks Pope Leo's first visit to an EU country outside Italy. During the Mass, he urged world leaders to stop dividing electorates and to respect every human being. The event is expected to be the largest gathering of his week-long visit to Spain.

cards.headline: Tata Steel Faces Delay on New Furnace Over Electrical Problem
cards.teaser: Plans for a 1.25 billion pound steel-making furnace may be postponed due to connectivity issues.
cards.body:
Tata Steel said its plans for a new 1.25 billion pound steel-making furnace may face delays due to an electrical connectivity problem. The company disclosed the potential setback as it works to resolve the infrastructure issue.

The furnace represents a major capital investment in steel production capacity. The electrical problem must be addressed before construction or commissioning can proceed on schedule.

cards.headline: CaaStle CEO Kept Job After Confessing to Fraud
cards.teaser: The fashion tech startup's board allowed Christine Hunsicker to remain in charge despite her admission.
cards.body:
Christine Hunsicker, chief executive of fashion tech startup CaaStle, confessed to defrauding the company. Despite her admission, the board allowed her to remain in her position.

During the company's final months, CaaStle conducted fraudulent audits and engaged in stock buybacks. Hunsicker led the damage control strategy while still serving as CEO.

cards.headline: Marks and Spencer Launches Training Program for 1,000 Young People
cards.teaser: The retail chain aims to address youth unemployment with a new traineeship scheme.
cards.body:
Marks and Spencer has launched a new traineeship program for 1,000 young people. The scheme directly addresses what the retailer identifies as a growing challenge: the number of young people not engaged in employment, education, or training.

The initiative reflects M&S's commitment to workforce development and creating clear pathways for young people to enter the job market through structured training opportunities.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Raises Questions About Retail Investor Access
cards.teaser: Analysts debate valuation and investment merits as the space company prepares to go public.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for what could be the largest initial public offering in history, with shares set to launch on June 12 at a $135 valuation. The company plans to sell 555.6 million shares, raising $75 billion from the offering.

A notable aspect of this IPO is the allocation reserved for individual investors. Up to a quarter of the shares will be available to retail buyers rather than institutional funds and banks—a significantly larger retail allocation than typical for major IPOs. This structure aims to broaden access to SpaceX shares beyond traditional investment institutions.

cards.teaser: The administration is considering plans to give Americans equity in artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump said a potential U.S. government equity stake in major AI companies could be beneficial, with discussions planned for the coming week. The administration is exploring how the government might acquire and distribute ownership stakes in artificial intelligence firms, allowing Americans to benefit financially from AI's success.

Senator Bernie Sanders has proposed that citizens own half of AI company equity as a public resource. Several approaches are being considered for how the government could structure such ownership arrangements.

cards.headline: Debt Collectors Face Verbal Abuse and Threats From Callers
cards.teaser: Workers in the industry endure harassment as more Americans fall behind on bills.
cards.body:
Debt collection workers frequently face verbal abuse and threats of violence from people they call about overdue bills. The problem has grown as more Americans take on debt and fall behind on payments.

The industry employs thousands of workers who contact consumers about unpaid obligations. These employees report experiencing a torrent of hostile responses, including threats, as economic pressures lead to increased delinquencies.

hero.headline: Lawsuit filed against AI gun detection company after school shooting
hero.body:
A survivor of a school shooting has filed a lawsuit against an AI gun detection firm after the company's system failed to identify a weapon before the attack occurred. The legal action raises questions about the reliability and accuracy standards required for artificial intelligence systems designed to detect threats in educational settings.

The lawsuit stems from an incident where the AI detection system was in place at the school but did not alert staff to the presence of a firearm. The technology, which uses artificial intelligence to scan for weapons, was intended to provide an additional layer of security for students and staff. The failure of the system to identify the weapon before the shooting has prompted legal scrutiny of the technology's effectiveness and the promises made by its manufacturer.

The case highlights broader concerns about the deployment of AI security systems in schools across the country. Many districts have invested in such technology as part of their safety protocols, relying on vendor claims about detection capabilities. The lawsuit questions what level of accuracy these systems must achieve before being deployed in environments where lives are at stake.

The legal action could have implications for the growing market of AI-based security technology in schools. Questions raised in the case include what standards these systems should meet, how they should be tested, and what responsibility manufacturers bear when their products fail to perform as advertised. The lawsuit also touches on whether schools adequately understand the limitations of the technology they purchase.

The outcome of this case may influence how schools evaluate and implement AI detection systems going forward. It could also prompt regulatory discussions about testing and certification requirements for security technology marketed to educational institutions. The gun detection industry has expanded rapidly in recent years as schools seek technological solutions to prevent violence, making the questions raised in this lawsuit relevant to many communities nationwide.

cards.headline: Bumblebees demonstrate problem-solving abilities comparable to larger animals
cards.teaser: Research shows bumblebees can solve problems spontaneously despite having small brains, challenging assumptions about intelligence and brain size.
cards.body:
Scientists have documented bumblebees solving complex problems without prior training, demonstrating cognitive abilities previously associated with animals like chimpanzees and elephants. The research challenges longstanding assumptions that advanced problem-solving requires large brains and shows that bees can approach tasks with spontaneous tool use and strategic thinking.

The findings suggest that brain size alone does not determine cognitive capability. Bumblebees accomplished tasks that require understanding cause and effect relationships, adapting their behavior to novel situations without being trained to do so. The research adds to growing evidence that insects possess more sophisticated mental abilities than previously recognized.

cards.headline: Apple's foldable iPhone may launch in limited color options
cards.teaser: Leaked information about Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone suggests the device may be available only in white or silver at launch.
cards.body:
New details about Apple's foldable iPhone design have emerged, with leakers suggesting the device may be offered exclusively in white or silver color options. Images shared by industry sources provide what is described as the clearest look yet at the design of the foldable device, which Apple is reportedly developing as part of its iPhone lineup.

The leak includes photographs showing the device in a white or silver finish. Multiple technology outlets have reported on the color limitation, noting it would represent a departure from Apple's typical practice of offering new flagship devices in multiple colors at launch. The device is part of Apple's broader push into foldable technology as competitors have already released folding smartphones.

cards.headline: Xbox holds annual games showcase with new leadership
cards.teaser: Microsoft's Xbox division presented its annual games showcase with Asha Sharma hosting the event for the first time as the division's leader.
cards.body:
Microsoft held its Xbox Games Showcase event, marking the first time Asha Sharma presented the annual announcement show in her role leading the division. The showcase featured upcoming game announcements and updates on previously revealed titles including Gears of War: E-Day and Fable.

The event drew attention across the gaming industry as observers looked for signals about Xbox's strategy under new leadership. Microsoft has been making decisions about game exclusivity and platform availability for its titles. The showcase included a separate presentation focused specifically on the Gears of War franchise.

cards.headline: Game developer Hideo Kojima expresses skepticism about AI in art
cards.teaser: The creator of Metal Gear Solid said he does not expect to see artificial intelligence create art during his lifetime and has no interest in using the technology.
cards.body:
Video game creator Hideo Kojima has stated he is not interested in using artificial intelligence for his work. While he acknowledges that AI might eventually create art, he expressed skepticism about witnessing that development during his lifetime.

Kojima, known for directing the Metal Gear Solid series and Death Stranding, shared his perspective as the gaming industry continues debating AI's role in creative fields. Some studios are experimenting with the technology for asset creation and other tasks, while others voice concerns about its impact on creative work and employment.

cards.headline: Vampire Survivors announces Nintendo Switch 2 version and expansion
cards.teaser: The indie game studio revealed plans for a Switch 2 version of its popular game along with new downloadable content and a Japanese studio.
cards.body:
Poncle, the developer of Vampire Survivors, announced the game will receive a Nintendo Switch 2 version alongside new downloadable content called Legacy Of The Bloodmoon. The studio also revealed plans to establish a Japanese development studio led by Sawaki Takeyasu, the artist known for work on Devil May Cry and El Shaddai.

The announcements came as part of a broader showcase of games. Vampire Survivors has been a commercial success for the indie studio since its original release. The expansion to Nintendo's next-generation hardware indicates continued support for the title across multiple platforms.

cards.headline: Ancient dragonflies grew to massive sizes in oxygen-rich atmosphere
cards.teaser: The largest insects ever recorded were dragonflies with wingspans exceeding two feet, sustained by an ancient atmosphere with oxygen levels higher than today.
cards.body:
Scientists have documented that the largest insects to ever exist were ancient dragonflies with wingspans of more than two feet. These massive creatures thrived in an atmosphere that contained significantly more oxygen than the air currently present on Earth.

The higher oxygen concentration in the ancient atmosphere allowed insects to grow to sizes that would be unsustainable in modern atmospheric conditions. Insects breathe through a system of tubes called tracheae, and the efficiency of this system depends on oxygen availability. The fossil record shows these giant dragonflies existed during a period when Earth's atmosphere had a much richer oxygen content than the roughly 21 percent present today.

hero.headline: Zverev and Cobolli meet in French Open final
hero.body:
Alexander Zverev and Flavio Cobolli are competing in the French Open men's singles final at Roland Garros, with both players appearing in their first Grand Slam final. The match marks a significant milestone for each competitor, as the winner will claim their maiden major title.

The two players have a prior history on the court. Five weeks before the final, Cobolli defeated Zverev in the semifinals at Munich, though Zverev reversed that result when they met subsequently in Madrid on a faster court surface. The clay at Roland Garros more closely resembles the conditions in Germany, which could influence how the match unfolds.

Cobolli has described reaching the final as an overwhelming emotional experience. The Italian player has never encountered a moment of this magnitude in his career, representing the biggest achievement of his life. His path through the tournament showcases his breakthrough performance at the highest level of professional tennis.

Zverev approaches the final after years of pursuing a Grand Slam title that has remained elusive throughout his career. The German player has had a favorable draw, becoming the first player since Mats Wilander in 1988 to face opponents in the round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals, and final who had never previously reached those stages. While Zverev has not played at his absolute best, he has been sufficiently strong against his opponents.

Analysts suggest that Zverev's ability to serve himself out of difficult situations may prove decisive. His capacity to retrieve balls could force Cobolli to take greater risks with his shot selection, either attempting winners or retreating into more conservative play. One tactical perspective suggests Cobolli should deploy drop shots and angled shots that force Zverev to move extensively, as Cobolli performs well at the net.

The final takes place on the clay courts of Roland Garros in Paris, where both players have navigated the grueling two-week tournament. The championship represents one of four Grand Slam tournaments in professional tennis, alongside the Australian Open, Wimbledon, and the US Open.

For both finalists, the match carries enormous significance. Victory will secure their place in tennis history and represent the pinnacle of professional achievement. Neither player has previously won at this level, and both understand that this opportunity may not present itself again soon. While Zverev could potentially reach another final relatively quickly, there remains no guarantee he will return to a Grand Slam championship match.

The final caps a tournament featuring compelling tennis across both men's and women's draws. One player will leave the court as a Grand Slam champion, while the other will face the disappointment of narrowly missing tennis's ultimate prize.

cards.headline: Brewers pitcher Misiorowski sets record with 103.7 mph pitch
cards.teaser: Milwaukee Brewers starter Jacob Misiorowski threw the fastest pitch ever recorded by a starting pitcher at 103.7 mph.
cards.body:
Jacob Misiorowski of the Milwaukee Brewers set a new record for the fastest pitch thrown by a starting pitcher, reaching 103.7 miles per hour. The rookie right-hander delivered 45 pitches at 101 mph or faster during his outing, a feat not accomplished by any pitcher since Bob Gibson in 1968. Misiorowski's performance came during a 7-1 victory at Coors Field, traditionally a challenging venue for pitchers.

The 21-year-old lowered his earned run average to 1.50 while making history with his velocity. Major League Baseball's official social media accounts acknowledged the record-breaking performance. The combination of sustained high velocity and effectiveness has marked Misiorowski's early career, drawing comparisons to historic pitching performances from decades past.

cards.headline: England defeats New Zealand by 115 runs in first Test at Lord's
cards.teaser: Gus Atkinson took five wickets on day four as England bowled out New Zealand in the morning session to win the opening Test and take a 1-0 series lead.
cards.body:
England claimed victory over New Zealand at Lord's, bowling out the tourists before lunch on day four. Gus Atkinson was the standout performer, finishing with five wickets for 30 runs as the bowlers dominated throughout the match. New Zealand, resuming at 55 for five and needing 199 runs, never threatened a comeback on a pitch that made batting extremely difficult.

The England bowlers proved ideally suited to exploit the Lord's surface, with Ollie Robinson leading the attack. New Zealand's batsmen struggled against the conditions, with only brief resistance from Devon Conway and Glenn Phillips in the second innings. The victory gives England a 1-0 lead in the three-match series and marks a strong start to their summer campaign.

cards.headline: Simone Biles reveals health scare
cards.teaser: Seven-time Olympic champion Simone Biles disclosed that she suffered a recent health scare, describing the experience as almost dying.
cards.body:
Seven-time Olympic champion Simone Biles has disclosed that she experienced a serious health scare, describing it as "almost dying." The gymnast made the revelation publicly, though further details about the specific nature of the incident have not been shared.

Biles has previously spoken openly about the physical and mental challenges of elite athletics throughout her career. The disclosure adds to her ongoing conversation about health and wellness in professional sports.

cards.headline: Germany defeats United States in pre-World Cup friendly
cards.teaser: Germany beat the United States in a warmup match ahead of the World Cup, though injuries to key players cast a shadow over the result.
cards.body:
Germany secured a victory over the United States in a pre-World Cup friendly match. The game served as preparation for both teams ahead of the tournament, allowing coaches to evaluate their squads before competition begins.

Injuries sustained during the match will likely force adjustments to both teams' World Cup plans. US coach Mauricio Pochettino expressed newfound excitement about the tournament for the United States, while observers highlighted the importance of the American back line's performance to the team's World Cup prospects.

cards.headline: Argentina rests Messi in Honduras friendly ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi sat out Argentina's match against Honduras as the team prepared for the upcoming World Cup.
cards.body:
Argentina rested Lionel Messi during a friendly against Honduras as part of the team's World Cup preparation. The decision reflects a cautious approach to managing the fitness of their star player ahead of the tournament.

Multiple nations used pre-World Cup friendlies to test tactics and build momentum. Brazil, Germany, Belgium, and Portugal each won their respective warm-up matches, allowing teams to finalize preparations before the competition begins.

cards.headline: Hatton and Vincent share lead at LIV Golf Andalucia
cards.teaser: Tyrrell Hatton and another player share the lead heading into the final round of LIV Golf Andalucia at Valderrama.
cards.body:
Tyrrell Hatton maintained his position at the top of the leaderboard heading into the final round of LIV Golf Andalucia. Hatton, who shared the lead after the opening round with Vincent, discussed his plans for managing what he described as disruptive crowds during play. The Crushers team led the team leaderboard after the first round at Valderrama.

Jon Rahm found his rhythm after a difficult start to the tournament, rebounding from being Valderramaed, a term referring to the course's challenging conditions. The 4Aces team made a significant move up the team leaderboard on moving day. The tournament features both individual and team competitions, with substantial prize money on offer for competitors.

hero.headline: Scott Pelley Calls for Removal of CBS News Chief Bari Weiss
hero.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent who spent decades at CBS News, was terminated by the network after a heated confrontation with executives over significant staff reductions at 60 Minutes, according to reporting by The Guardian.

The conflict emerged following CBS News management's decision to fire the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi, without providing specific reasons for the terminations. During a Monday morning meeting with newly appointed executive editor Nick Bilton and other CBS News leadership, Pelley expressed his frustration with Bari Weiss, the former opinion commentator who joined the network in October as editor-in-chief.

"She's murdering 60 Minutes," Pelley said during the meeting, according to The Guardian. "She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that."

Weiss conveyed to Pelley that his behavior during the meeting was inappropriate. Pelley subsequently told staff members he expected to be fired. On Tuesday evening, Bilton sent Pelley a termination message, citing his conduct in the meeting.

"Yesterday, you hijacked my first meeting with staff to disparage me, my qualifications, and my intentions with remarkable incivility and contempt," Bilton wrote in the message obtained by Puck's Dylan Byers.

Bilton also notified 60 Minutes staff of Pelley's departure, stating he had made repeated attempts to have direct conversations with Pelley over the weekend. "I made repeated attempts to have direct conversations with him over the weekend, and this afternoon I tried to find common ground. That was not the path Scott chose," Bilton wrote.

Pelley later issued a public statement accusing the network's new executives of silencing employees and claiming they instructed him "to inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He emphasized that 60 Minutes had maintained its position as America's top program "because our beloved audience finds integrity, quality, and humanity in our stories."

The termination represents a significant shift at the storied news program. With Anderson Cooper announcing his departure earlier this year and Pelley now fired, 60 Minutes is left with only three full-time correspondents: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and Jon Wertheim. Norah O'Donnell contributes to the show as well.

The controversy comes months after David Ellison's Skydance acquired CBS's parent company Paramount. In December, Pelley had publicly praised the new management's approach to 60 Minutes, stating the show experienced "no corporate interference of any kind." Nine days later, Alfonsi revealed that Weiss had spiked her investigation into an El Salvador prison for "political" reasons, triggering one of the biggest controversies in the network's history.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner Wed in Sicily
cards.teaser: The singer and actor married in Sicily, with Elton John performing at the ceremony.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and Callum Turner married in Sicily in a ceremony that featured a performance by Elton John. The musician serenaded the couple with his song Your Song during the celebration.

The wedding took place in Palermo, where the couple's choice of location sparked local discussion. The pair had previously held wedding celebrations in London before traveling to Italy for the Sicily ceremony.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Returns to Touring After Six Years
cards.teaser: The pop star performed her first headlining concert since 2019, launching the Eternal Sunshine tour in Oakland.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande launched her Eternal Sunshine tour at Oakland Arena on Saturday night, marking her first headlining concert in six and a half years. The performance showcased material from her recent work rather than a greatest hits compilation.

Grande deliberately crafted the setlist to create a meaningful dialogue with her audience, prioritizing newer songs over fan favorites from earlier in her career. The tour opener represented a significant return for the pop artist after her last performances in 2019.

cards.headline: Tribeca Festival Condemns Joke About Palestinian Rape Made on Red Carpet
cards.teaser: The film festival criticized remarks by comedian Elon Gold and influencer Lizzy Savetsky at a premiere.
cards.body:
The Tribeca Festival condemned jokes made by comedian Elon Gold and influencer Lizzy Savetsky on the red carpet of The Wedding Entertainer. A video clip shared on social media showed the pair making offensive remarks about Palestinian rape.

The festival issued a statement calling the remarks unacceptable, emphasizing that human suffering should never be mocked. The clip drew widespread criticism after circulating online following the film premiere event.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center Lawsuit Against Musician Dismissed
cards.teaser: A judge threw out the Kennedy Center's case against a musician who canceled a performance over a Trump naming dispute.
cards.body:
A judge dismissed a lawsuit filed by the Kennedy Center against musician Chuck Redd, who canceled a Christmas Eve performance. The cancellation came amid a dispute over naming related to former President Trump.

The court sided with Redd in the case brought by the Washington arts venue. The Kennedy Center had sued after Redd pulled out of the scheduled holiday concert.

cards.headline: Tony Awards Set for Ceremony With No Clear Favorites
cards.teaser: The Broadway awards show will take place following a record season, with competitive races across categories.
cards.body:
The Tony Awards will cap a record Broadway season with no clear front-runners in key categories. The ceremony features 26 award categories, with predictions divided among competing productions.

Shows featuring vampires, literary adaptations, and other varied productions are competing for recognition. The awards follow what industry observers describe as a highly successful season for Broadway theater.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Cancels Second Pittsburgh Concert
cards.teaser: The country singer called off a show at Acrisure Stadium, citing severe weather concerns.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen canceled a second scheduled concert in Pittsburgh due to the threat of severe weather. The show at Acrisure Stadium was called off days after the singer had an onstage incident at another performance.

Wallen addressed what he called nonsense rumors surrounding the cancellation, attributing the decision to weather conditions. A local baseball team offered free admission to fans who had tickets to the canceled concert.

hero.headline: Trump says Iran peace deal stalled as negotiations continue
hero.body:
President Trump said Iran has not agreed to a deal to end the ongoing conflict because the country is strong and proud, but indicated Tehran will ultimately have to reach an agreement. "They're strong, they're proud, there are things they never thought they'd be doing that they're going to have to do," Trump said, suggesting Iran has no choice but to accept terms in negotiations aimed at ending hostilities between the United States and Iran.

The president acknowledged the difficulty of the diplomatic process without specifying what leverage or circumstances would force Tehran to the negotiating table. Trump stated the deal would either be "great and meaningful, or there will be no deal at all."

Iran's negotiating team has taken a more cautious stance about the talks. Esmail Baghaei, the spokesperson for Iran's negotiating team, said that while negotiators have reached conclusions on many issues, an agreement is not imminent. "It is correct to say that we have reached a conclusion on a large portion of the issues under discussion. But to say that this means the signing of an agreement is imminent – no one can make such a claim," Baghaei said at a foreign ministry press briefing.

Baghaei also pointed to confusion in American positions and Israeli interference as obstacles to reaching a deal. He insisted that a ceasefire in Lebanon must be included in any memorandum of understanding that would lead to Iran allowing commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the United States lifting its blockade of Iranian ports. Regarding the strait, Baghaei clarified that discussions centered on "fees for navigational services" rather than tolls.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed more optimism about the negotiations. "There were some talks going on in Qatar today, so we'll see if we can make progress. I think it's a lot of talking back and forth going on about specific language in the initial document," Rubio told reporters in Jaipur during an official visit to India. He added that the Strait of Hormuz would open "one way or another."

The conflict between the United States and Iran has created significant diplomatic and logistical challenges extending beyond the negotiating table. These complications have affected international events, including the World Cup, which begins Thursday. FIFA declined Iran's request to relocate its group stage matches from U.S. stadiums to venues in Canada or Mexico.

Iranians are largely banned from traveling to the United States under current restrictions. The Iranian soccer team will have to fly in and out of the country for each match without overnight stays, creating an exhausting schedule for the three group stage games on U.S. soil.

The negotiations represent a test of whether diplomatic channels can resolve the conflict between Washington and Tehran while addressing the humanitarian and logistical consequences of the ongoing tension.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official secured the Democratic nomination and could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Deb Haaland, who served as an official in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. The victory positions her to potentially make history in the general election.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in United States history. She will face the Republican nominee in the race to lead New Mexico.

cards.headline: California governor primary results show Hilton, Becerra leading
cards.teaser: Democrats and Republicans are selecting nominees to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton leads the Republican field while Xavier Becerra is ahead among Democrats in California's primary race for governor. The election will determine who advances to face off in November as a replacement for Governor Gavin Newsom.

On the Democratic side, Becerra is competing against Katie Porter and Tom Steyer. The Republican candidates include Hilton and Chad Bianco. Primary results were still being counted as votes continued to be tallied.

cards.headline: Influencers use prediction markets on X to question election results
cards.teaser: Posts about prediction markets are becoming a tool to spread doubt about election outcomes.
cards.body:
Influencers on X are increasingly using prediction markets as a vehicle to raise questions about election results. The posts represent a new method for spreading skepticism about electoral outcomes on the social media platform.

Prediction markets, which allow users to bet on political outcomes, are being referenced in posts designed to sow distrust. The trend reflects how different tools and data sources can be deployed to challenge election integrity on social media.

cards.headline: Maine prepares for primary as California counts votes
cards.teaser: An upcoming primary election in Maine follows last week's voting in California.
cards.body:
Maine voters will head to the polls for a primary election, with the Platner race drawing attention. The election continues the active campaign season that has intensified across multiple states.

California is still tallying results from its primary election held last week. The ongoing vote counting and upcoming Maine contest reflect the intensity of the current election cycle as candidates compete for nominations ahead of general elections.

cards.headline: Trump administration uses compliance rules to shape higher education
cards.teaser: Reporting and compliance mechanisms allow federal control over colleges without legislative approval.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is using compliance and reporting requirements to exercise control over how colleges and universities operate, according to an analysis of federal higher education policy. These mechanisms allow the government to shape institutional decisions without securing congressional legislation or generating public debate.

The compliance schemes affect multiple aspects of college operations, including governance, admissions, hiring practices, curriculum, research activities, and definitions of educational quality. While these requirements operate below the radar of most public attention, they collectively have significant impact on how higher education institutions function and make decisions.

cards.headline: AI business faces profitability and infrastructure challenges
cards.teaser: Investors confronted with high costs, weak returns, and infrastructure concerns about artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
The artificial intelligence industry faces four fundamental challenges that may reshape investor expectations. CEOs and Microsoft have said AI is proving too expensive to implement, while a Bain study found the technology is not generating the financial returns companies anticipated.

Infrastructure demand for AI remains strong but fell short of the most optimistic projections, as shown by Broadcom's forecast that some analysts characterized as weak. Financing AI infrastructure is expected to remain expensive for an extended period, with indicators suggesting the Federal Reserve may keep interest rates elevated longer than previously expected.
